disposition_reason: Pb, Cd, Hg, Sn, Al, Cr, Fe, Zn and Cu were measured in 45 canned fish, meat and vegetable or legume samples from Lebanese supermarkets; Tables 4-6 give mean ± SD and range per category and type.

study.design: Market survey of 45 canned foods of different brands and countries, plus XRF of can metal composition
study.origin: fish all imported (Thailand, Vietnam, Morocco, Denmark); meats from Holland, KSA, Lebanon, China, France, Denmark, Spain; vegetables imported (China, Peru, Egypt, Thailand, France, Dubai) and legumes largely manufactured in Lebanon
study.method: Drained, homogenized; H2O2/HNO3 digestion; GF-AAS for Cd, Cr, Cu, Fe, Pb, Zn; ICP-MS for Al, Hg, Sn; handheld XRF for cans
study.qa: CRMs NIST 1573a tomato leaves and NIST 1556b oyster tissue in triplicate, recoveries 94-102%

controls.comparator: canned fish and meat in lower-tin or lacquered cans
controls.outcome: Sn mean 63.50 µg/g in canned vegetables (unlacquered, high-Sn cans) vs 0.76 µg/g in canned fish and 2.40 µg/g in canned meat; authors report a correlation of can Sn and Al with food Sn and Al

unresolved: Number of samples per food type (luncheon meat, hot dogs, liver paste, vegetables, legumes) not stated; category n derived from the Methods (14 fish, 11 meat, 20 vegetables and legumes).
Table 6 meat Hg mean printed '0.046-0.024'; text says 0.045 µg/g. Table 5 vegetables Cr SD printed '0.0.02'.
Oyster CRM Hg certified and found values (368±7, 353±25) duplicate the tomato Fe row; Hg recovery for that CRM unclear.
Per-sample Sn and Cd values in Figures 1 and 2 are bar labels in figures and not recorded.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: EU maximum levels cited: Pb 0.1 µg/g vegetables and meat, 0.2 µg/g legumes, 0.3 µg/g fish and mushroom; Cd 0.1 µg/g; Hg 0.5 µg/g fish; Sn 200 µg/g canned food
regulatory_or_exposure.value: 30% of vegetables and legumes and 45% of fish samples above Cd 0.1 µg/g; 15% of vegetable and legume cans above Pb limit

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Hypothetical weekly Cd intake from one high-Cd can of each food per week
regulatory_or_exposure.value: 337 µg/week, 4.8 µg/kg bw/week, about 2 times the EFSA TWI 2.5 µg/kg bw
